title: Chapter XXXVI
summary: Jane follows the mysterious call back toward Thornfield, now traveling freely with money, family, and a home behind her. She finds the Hall exactly as her dream foretold: a roofless, blackened ruin. An innkeeper explains that Bertha escaped, burned Thornfield, and leapt from its roof. Rochester saved the servants and attempted to save Bertha, but the collapsing house cost him a hand and his sight. Having withdrawn to isolated Ferndean, he remains alive; Jane immediately orders transport to him.
events: Jane independently leaves Moor House to make personal inquiry about Rochester.
She discovers that Thornfield has been destroyed by fire.
Bertha set the fire and died by jumping from the roof as Rochester approached her.
Rochester's rescue effort left him blind and without one hand; Jane sets out for Ferndean.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Returns by free choice rather than need, able to learn the truth before deciding what relationship she wants.

characters.name: Edward Rochester
characters.development: Acts courageously toward servants and Bertha, surviving humbled, disabled, and isolated after losing Thornfield.

characters.name: Bertha Mason Rochester
characters.development: Destroys the house that confined her and dies in the conflagration, ending the legal marriage.

threads.text: Jane's dream of ruined Thornfield becomes literal.
Bertha's confinement and Rochester's existing marriage end in fire and death.
Rochester is now legally free but physically dependent and socially withdrawn.
